title: SLO Targets – Benchmark Data Extract (Q4 2025–Q1 2026)
content:
Purpose
- Snapshot of historical reliability/latency distributions used to propose initial SLO targets for Hosted API vs Dedicated tiers.
- Intended to support: (a) target-setting discussions, (b) backtesting candidate burn-rate alert thresholds, (c) identifying obvious regional/model outliers.

Coverage / time range
- Time range analyzed: 2025-10-01 through 2026-01-31 (inclusive)
- Aggregation: daily rollups for percentiles + full-window aggregates for headline numbers
- Data sources: gateway request metrics (HTTP), routing service metrics, runtime token streaming metrics, scheduler readiness metrics (Dedicated)

Key definitions (quick)
- "Success" for chat/completions:
  - Non-streaming: HTTP 2xx with non-empty completion; excludes 4xx (auth/validation) from denominator
  - Streaming: stream opened successfully AND server completed stream without server-side disconnect; client abort tracked separately
- Latency SLIs:
  - Non-streaming: end-to-end request latency (gateway) p95/p99
  - Streaming: (1) TTFT (time-to-first-token) p95/p99, (2) stream duration p95/p99 (from first byte to stream end)
- Error rates:
  - 5xx_rate: fraction of requests returning 5xx (gateway)
  - timeout_rate: server-side timeouts (gateway + routing enforced deadlines), excludes customer-side timeouts when attributable
  - disconnect_rate_streaming: server-side streaming disconnects / streams opened

Exclusions / adjustments applied
- Excluded from denominators:
  - 401/403 invalid auth
  - 404 unknown route/model
  - 429 rate-limit responses (tracked separately; not counted as "availability" errors for this extract)
  - 4xx validation errors (bad params, schema errors)
- Dedicated-specific:
  - When tier=dedicated, requests served via customer-pinned pools only (no spillover); failures due to customer-specified config mis-match excluded (very small)
- Maintenance windows:
  - Scheduled maintenance windows were NOT removed (we want to capture customer-perceived experience). Planned work should be visible and managed via budgets.

Known caveats
- Sampling: high-volume Hosted streaming metrics use 1:10 sampling on some routes in us-east-1 and us-west-2; percentiles are approximate. Nadia/Logan validated approx error vs logs on two representative days.
- Cardinality: per-model per-route breakdown is partial; the model field is normalized to "model_family" for certain hot endpoints to keep cost down (see notes below).
- Attribution: client abort vs server disconnect classification changed mid-window (gateway change landed 2026-01-08). Pre-01-08 disconnect splits should be treated as directional only.

TAB: README – column dictionary
- tier: hosted | dedicated
- region: us-east-1 | us-west-2 | eu-west-1
- endpoint_group:
  - chat_streaming ("/v1/chat/completions" with stream=true)
  - chat_nonstreaming ("/v1/chat/completions" with stream=false)
  - embeddings ("/v1/embeddings")
- model_family: normalized model identifier used in dashboards
- n_requests: count of requests in window (post-exclusion)
- n_streams_opened: count of streams opened (streaming only)
- availability_success_rate: 1 - (5xx + server_timeouts + server_disconnects) / denom
- http_5xx_rate: 5xx / denom
- server_timeout_rate: timeouts / denom
- server_disconnect_rate: server disconnects / streams_opened (streaming only)
- latency_ms_p50/p95/p99: end-to-end gateway latency (non-streaming + embeddings)
- ttft_ms_p50/p95/p99: time-to-first-token (streaming)
- stream_duration_ms_p50/p95/p99: stream duration (streaming)

TAB: DEDICATED_POOL_READINESS – proposed readiness SLI support
Columns: date | region | pool_group | readiness_success_rate | minutes_below_99_5 | minutes_below_99_0 | notes

Definition used here (draft): readiness_success_rate = 1 - (minutes with scheduler_unavailable OR allocatable_tokens_per_s < configured_floor) / total_minutes
- scheduler_unavailable: scheduler health check failed OR zero schedulable GPU slots across pool
- allocatable_tokens_per_s: scheduler capacity signal normalized to customer-configured min throughput

2025-10-05 | us-east-1 | dedicated-prod (aggregate) | 99.980% | 6 | 1 | One AZ maintenance + delayed reschedule
2025-11-28 | us-west-2 | dedicated-prod (aggregate) | 99.910% | 38 | 12 | Autoscaler lag after node drain; impacted 2 large customers; see Dedicated escalation notes
2026-01-17 | us-west-2 | dedicated-prod (aggregate) | 99.950% | 21 | 3 | Capacity dip; mitigated by scaling policy change
2026-01-29 | eu-west-1 | dedicated-prod (aggregate) | 99.990% | 2 | 0 | Stable

TAB: MODEL NORMALIZATION NOTES
We could not safely retain full model_id for all endpoints without exceeding label cardinality budgets.
- For hosted chat_streaming: model_family is one of:
  - rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct
  - rw-mistral-8x7b-instruct
  - rw-qwen2.5-72b-instruct
  - other (collapsed)
- For dedicated: model_family collapsed to "customer-pinned (mixed)" for this extract. Customer-by-customer cuts are in a restricted sheet (not in this shared file) due to leakage risk.

Methodology (how this was computed)
1) Pull request counts/errors from gateway metrics
   - Metric family: api_gateway.requests
   - Group by: tier, region, endpoint_group, model_family
   - Denominator: requests excluding 4xx/auth/rate-limit as defined above
2) Pull streaming TTFT and stream duration from runtime/gateway streaming metrics
   - Metric family: runtime.stream.ttft_ms, runtime.stream.duration_ms (percentiles)
   - Join on: tier, region, model_family
   - Caveat: for high-volume routes, percentiles are computed from histogram buckets with sampling
3) Compute availability_success_rate
   - availability = 1 - (5xx + server_timeouts + server_disconnects) / denom
   - For streaming, server_disconnects is used; client abort is excluded (tracked separately and used for product guidance, not reliability SLO)
4) Dedicated readiness
   - From scheduler metrics: scheduler.health, scheduler.allocatable_capacity
   - Aggregated to per-minute time series, then rolled to daily readiness

Interpretation notes / what this implies for target proposals (draft)
- Hosted streaming success rates are consistently around ~99.90–99.94% by region for the top model family; tail events are mostly disconnect/timeouts rather than 5xx.
- Dedicated success rates are higher in this window (~99.96–99.97%), but readiness dips in us-west-2 are the main driver of customer-visible incidents.
- Embeddings are strong and stable; most of the budget would be consumed by rare infra/network timeout events.
- Latency targets should be tiered and endpoint-specific. TTFT behaves differently than non-streaming p95.

Open questions (to resolve before final SLO target lock)
- Do we set streaming latency SLO on TTFT only, or TTFT + stream duration? (Current recommendation: TTFT primary, stream duration secondary / diagnostic)
- Should 429 be included in availability for Hosted? (Currently excluded; product wants separate "throttle" indicator)
- Dedicated readiness paging policy: page on sustained readiness dips (<99.5% daily projected), or ticket-first unless customer impact confirmed?
- After 2026-01-08 disconnect reclassification, do we re-baseline targets using only post-change data?
